audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows contradict the page's own why-text. The chart reads Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir/Skill/Skill for rows 0-4 while whys[0..4] every one of them describe the stage as Lillia's.
audit.why: The packet chart is Lillia for rows 0-4 and Vladimir for rows 5-6 — an exact match for the prose. A 450-range kiter stacking move speed does not lose Levels 2-3 to a 600-range melee drain.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 flipped to Lillia as five matched full/content pairs in one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the Level 6 spike treated Lilting Lullaby as an unconditional threat.
audit.why: Lilting Lullaby is 150s at rank 1 and, per Riot's text, only affects enemies who already have Dream Dust on them — it is conditional on her having landed a spell on you first. That condition is the entire level-6 interaction and it was missing.
audit.corrected: The Dream Dust prerequisite and the 150s cooldown written into spikes[1].text and the cooldown block, with Q 6s, W 14s and E 12s alongside.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors in the same sentence: the page says 'she out-sustains your Q with her passive true-damage burn ticks'. Dream-Laden Bough is a max-health damage-over-time effect — it does no healing at all — and the true damage in her kit belongs to the outer edge of Blooming Blows, not the passive.
audit.why: A player reading this waits out a heal that does not exist, and stacks MR against damage that is actually true on the Q edge. Getting the true-damage source right is what tells you resistances are the wrong buy.
audit.corrected: Passive restated as a max-health burn that damages rather than heals; true damage moved to the Blooming Blows edge in spikes[0].text, early, wants.foe[1] and the cooldown block.
sources: enemyKit Q text and trueDamage flag

audit.why: suspectNames flagged 'Her Lilting Lullaby' in spikes[1] as a probable wrong name (distance 4). It is a false positive — Lilting Lullaby is Lillia's real R name in Riot's data.
audit.corrected: No change on that ground; the string was rewritten for the Dream Dust condition instead.

edits.before: - Lillia Blooming Blows: matchup-defining — Her kite + move speed stacks. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Blooming Blows: 6s, stacking move speed, true damage on the edge. - Watch Out! Eep!: 14s. - Swirlseed: 12s, 700 range, rolls until it hits. - Lilting Lullaby: 150s, and it needs Dream Dust on you first.

edits.before: Her kite + move speed stacks. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 6s cooldown, stacking move speed — engage when she has spent it.

edits.before: Lillia kites you all through the early game. Her Q (Blooming Blows) gives movement speed per hit and her W (Watch Out! Eep!) pokes from range, so she pelts you and skips away before your E stacks land. You can't close the gap without pooling forward, and she out-sustains your Q with her passive true-damage burn ticks.
edits.after: Lillia kites you all through the early game. Blooming Blows is a 6s cooldown that stacks move speed and deals true damage on its outer edge, and Watch Out! Eep! pokes from 500 range, so she skips away before your E lands. Her passive is a max-health burn — it damages you, it does not heal her.

edits.before: Her Lilting Lullaby is the danger, not yours — a landed R sleeps you for a burst follow-up. Your Hemoplague is fine but doesn't win the level-6 window outright because she's mobile and hard to pin. Hold pool for the moment she R's you so you can cleanse the setup by repositioning.
edits.after: Lilting Lullaby only touches enemies already carrying Dream Dust, so if none of her spells have hit you, her 150s ultimate does nothing to you at all. Take the poke seriously for that reason alone: stay unhit before 6 and her ultimate has no target to land on.

edits.before: Lillia owns the early lane by kiting: Blooming Blows stacks move speed so she dances out of your E range, and Watch Out! Eep! pokes you from distance while her passive burn out-sustains your Transfusion. You physically can't pin her without wasting pool, so just farm, eat minimal poke, and accept the level 1-5 disadvantage.
edits.after: Lillia owns the early lane by kiting: Blooming Blows stacks move speed so she dances out of your 600 E range, and Watch Out! Eep! pokes from 500 while her passive burns a share of your max health. You can't pin her without wasting a 28s pool, so farm, eat minimal poke, and accept the level 1-5 deficit.

edits.before: Land the R sleep to burst you with her true-damage passive
edits.after: Chip you with any spell so Dream Dust makes you R-able

notes: I did not act on the 'terrain-cuts-retreat' missing interaction. Riot's Swirlseed text says the seed rolls until it hits a wall or target — it does not create terrain, so the derived terrain flag looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire, and the mirror reached the same conclusion independently. Writing 'hold Flash for the wall' would have shipped an invented mechanic. The revealsStealth flag on the same ability is unsupported by the text too. The page also uses 'his' and 'he' for Lillia across roughly ten template strings; not fixed here for length-budget reasons but worth a mechanical pass.
